assessment: Pin1 is an essential prolyl cis/trans isomerase which has attracted considerable attention as this enzyme family is implicated in cancer and neurodegenerative diseases. Here, authors provide compelling evidence that Pin1 modulates the activity of an important cell signaling kinase, Protein Kinase C by a non-catalytic mechanism. This result suggests a new mode of Pin1 action, regulating the cellular stability of the kinase via a chaperone-like activity.
